title: Maximum residue levels for ametoctradin
summary: EU discusses increases in MRLs for ametoctradin on certain animal products
update: The European Union (EU) is discussing an increase in the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for ametoctradin on certain animal products.
impacted_products: Products of animal origin (swine, cattle, sheep, goat, horse)
what_changing: The EU is discussing an increase in the MRLs for ametoctradin on certain animal products as summarised in Table 1.
why: The European Food Safety Authority carried out a periodic review of the MRLs for ametoctradin (under Regulation 396/2005 , Art. 12), and reviewed additional data from an applicant requesting modification of the existing MRLs ( EFSA 2020 ; EFSA 2026 ). The request for an increase in MRLs on certain livestock products was supported by the data, and the existing MRLs were considered to be safe for consumers.
timeline: The new MRLs are expected to apply from early 2027.
background: MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database . For further information on the setting of import tolerances, see Pesticide residue import tolerance MRLs explained .
resources: EFSA (2020) Review of the existing maximum residue levels for ametoctradin according to Article 12 of Regulation (EC) No 396/2005 . EFSA Journal, 18(1): 5990. EFSA (2026) Evaluation of confirmatory data following the Article 12 MRL review for ametoctradin . EFSA Journal, 24(1): e9829.
